title: Format Traps: Points-League Players and 9-Cat Fluff
brief: Which players are likely mispriced in our room because their value comes from points-league scoring or from inflated 9-cat totals, and which are undervalued for a category league? Tiers must separate players to avoid at market price from players to target.
summary: Yahoo prices in our room mix points and category drafts. That pushes up scoring-first guards and forwards such as Cunningham, Jalen Johnson, Giddey, Brunson, Sengun and Siakam, plus 9-cat "fluff" players such as Holmgren and Bridges, so let others pay market price for them. Your auction money is better spent on category players the market underprices, such as Alexander-Walker, Daniels, Jaren Jackson, White, George, Reid and Davis, at the expert prices given below.

paragraphs.text: Yahoo ADP mixes owners drafting for points with owners drafting for categories. Players who are valued in points leagues can show up high in category draft rooms and at the top of autodraft queues. Our auction runs on Yahoo, so expect those players to be nominated early and bid up.

The edge is the gap between a player's points value and his category value. When the site ranks or prices a player for the other format, he is mispriced for us. That works both ways. Let points-driven prices go by, and target category players the market prices as if this were a points league.

What to check before each bid: is the player tagged as a points-league player or as 9-cat fluff, and how far is the Yahoo average cost above the experts' category price? If the gap is large, set your maximum at the expert price and stop there. Jalen Johnson shows the pattern. Both sites price him as a first-rounder, but experts see a mid second-rounder in 9-cat, so 35 to 40 USD is our ceiling.

Some players get most of their value from scoring, with weak defensive stats and lower efficiency. They are better in points leagues than in category leagues. A high-usage scorer with few other strengths can be top 10 in points leagues but only a third-rounder in categories. In 9-cat, efficiency, assists, steals and blocks carry more weight.

The early-round traps in our room are these. Cunningham: experts value him at 45 to 50 USD and 8th to 10th in categories, and his 3.9 turnovers point to a punt TO build. Giddey: a pick in the 20s for categories, about 29 to 31 USD. Brunson: a fourth-round category player, worth about 20 to 25 USD in a punt BLK build, so let others pay 30 USD or more. Sengun: do not chase above about 30 USD. Sabonis: round 3 for categories, about 24 to 26 USD.

Siakam is the clearest mid-round trap. Experts put him at 50 to 60 in categories, and they expect his assists and usage to drop with Haliburton back. Prices near last season's 25 USD in our league are bust prices. Late in the draft, pay only a few USD for Castle, about 1 to 2 USD for Dybantsa as a punt TO bench piece, and no more than about 10 USD for Zion.

A points tag does not always mean avoid. Adebayo in the mid 20s USD, Mobley in the mid to high 20s, Jaylen Brown near 23 USD, Banchero at 13 to 20 USD, Randle at 10 to 12 USD and Gobert at 8 to 12 USD all match the experts' category prices. Buy them at those levels for the punt build each one fits.

sections.heading: 9-cat fluff: pay for the per-game line

paragraphs.text: Standard 9-cat rankings use Z-scores that include turnovers. They make some players look better than they really are, and those players get overdrafted. In our data the inflation comes from three sources: low turnovers (Jarrett Allen), blocks (Holmgren), and season totals built on games played (Bridges, Sheppard).

Concrete caps: Holmgren at about 21 to 22 USD, not 30 USD, and check his quadriceps status before 2026-10-18. Bridges: only a few USD, because his per-game line was at waiver level late last season. Allen: near 13 to 14 USD, not prices driven by ESPN. Zubac: 10 to 14 USD, and let someone else pay 20 USD. Okongwu: a mid-priced second center, not a round 4 value. Sheppard: 1 to 5 USD as a late flier.

In H2H we win weekly per-game production, not season totals. In the first two weeks, check minutes and shot volume for these players. Bridges and Sheppard need minutes to justify a roster spot. If they are not getting them, use the waiver wire, which allows up to 6 adds per week.

These are the best targets. Alexander-Walker: a top 35 to 50 category player with no weak category, and bids up to about 20 USD are supported. Daniels: a steals outlier worth 18 to 24 USD. Jaren Jackson: a strong buy in the high teens USD. White: a bargain in the mid teens. George: experts expect a top 40 per-game return, and 13 to 20 USD is fine. Reid: 10 to 14 USD. Murphy: about the mid 20s USD, with no weak category, and his points-league complaints do not apply to us.

At the top of the draft, Giannis is a clear top 5 category pick. Plan to spend around 60 to 62 USD and punt FT%. Durant is fair in the low 40s USD, and the 50 USD range is a stretch. Amen Thompson is fair up to the high 30s, Reaves at 30 to 36 USD, and Curry in the mid to high 20s if you accept his knee risk. Davis is worth a bid into the mid 20s USD. Let him go if the room chases last season's 54 USD.

A category tag alone does not make a player cheap. Haliburton is not top 10 in Yahoo points, but experts cap him near 35 USD, below his Yahoo cost. Knueppel's market rank in the 30s and 40s is too high, so stay around 8 to 12 USD. At the cheap end, bid up to about 8 USD for Ty Jerome, about 6 USD for McDaniels and about 11 USD for Caleb Wilson. Ware is worth up to about 13 USD.

The fluff label is not settled. Lloyd says nine-cat rankings inflate Okongwu, yet Yahoo values him at 22 USD and an expert mock paid 16 USD. Sharpe is flagged as a per-minute fluff case, but one expert mock paid 10 USD for him and still called that below his value. Jaylen Brown and Banchero are tagged as points-league players, but the notes also say 9-cat rankings undervalue them. Banchero was 125th in nine-cat but 58th in head-to-head last season. Amen Thompson splits the experts too: most value him at 35 to 40 USD, while Lloyd sees a third-rounder (about 28 to 30) if his blocks and FG% do not come back. In practice, pay the lower figure. Let early-season minutes and per-game stats decide whether these players are worth holding.
